hormuz.label: Gulf shipping risk
hormuz.value: Reported attacks threaten Gulf energy infrastructure

facts.text: Nov 12: Houthis said they targeted Saudi pipeline, Yanbu and Riyadh sites. The Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting two drones.
Iran said four tankers were hit in Hormuz; Reuters could not independently verify that account.

hormuz.say: Reported attacks threaten export infrastructure; the tanker account remains unverified.

aicapex.label: AI capex boom
aicapex.value: AI investment needs cash, debt and equity

facts.text: Oct 29: Amazon kept 2026 cash capex guidance near $220B. Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was an outflow of $42.4B, largely reflecting AI investment.
Meta guides 2026 capex of $135–145B; Q3 free cash flow was negative $2.12B.
Oct 26: Meta launched approximately $35B of equity offerings, alongside plans for a future $60B at-the-market program.
Nov 10: Anthropic filed a preliminary IPO prospectus for 825 million shares at an estimated $70-78 each. Terms remain subject to completion.

aicapex.say: The builders are still investing heavily, but cash generation and financing terms matter as much as growth.

oil.label: Oil

facts.text: Nov 12 futures: Brent settled at $95.82, up 3.3%; WTI at $88.74, up 2.6%.
Both benchmarks were still down about 2.5% for the week. The session's rebound followed the reported Houthi attacks.

oil.say: Brent rose 3.3% on Nov 12, while remaining down about 2.5% for the week.

inflation.label: Inflation pressure

facts.text: Oct 2026 CPI rose 0.4% m/m; core rose 0.3%. Missing Oct 2025 data prevent most 12-month comparisons. Released Nov 10.
September PCE inflation was 3.6% year over year; core PCE was 3.1%. Released Oct 29.
November preliminary Michigan expectations: year-ahead 4.3%, versus October's 4.7%; long-run 3.4%, versus 3.5%.
September Canadian CPI: 3.1% year over year; 2.2% excluding gasoline.

inflation.say: Energy still lifts headline inflation, even as household inflation expectations ease.

issuance.label: AI capital supply
issuance.value: AI capital demand spans debt, equity and customer cash

facts.text: Nov 3: Meta said it was raising $15B through a five-part US dollar bond offering to help finance AI infrastructure.
CoreWeave's Sep 30 debt carrying values totalled $46.873B, rounded to $46.9B: current and non-current recourse plus non-recourse debt, excluding leases.
Nov 4: Treasury announced $125B of refunding securities, replacing about $97B of maturities and raising about $28B of new cash.
Nov 10: Anthropic proposed an IPO and a $26B concurrent private placement, contingent on completion of the offering.

issuance.say: AI funding uses debt and equity; CoreWeave's reported debt also shows why financing terms matter.

overcap.label: AI build-out risk
overcap.value: Investors question AI build-out pace and returns

facts.text: Nov 5: investors feared a Democratic-controlled Congress could slow data-center construction, triggering a sharp AI stock selloff.
Nov 3: JPMorgan vice chairman Daniel Pinto said AI revenue and earnings expectations were too steep and could correct.
Counterpoint: Blackstone president Jon Gray said compute demand still ran well ahead of supply; he also said higher capital costs would slow the pace.

overcap.say: Build-out and payoff fears are investor concerns; strong compute demand remains a counterpoint.

fed.label: Fed

facts.text: Oct 28: the Fed held at 3.75–4.00%, by a 10–2 vote. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack preferred a quarter-point increase.
Nov 6: October payrolls rose 165,000 and unemployment was 4.1%.
Nov 12: WSJ reported a Treasury selloff as Fed officials discussed reducing inflation through higher interest rates.
The next scheduled FOMC decision is Dec 9, following the Dec 8–9 meeting.

fed.say: The Fed held in October; November inflation and rate expectations keep another hike in focus.

y10.label: US 10-yr yield

facts.text: Treasury par curve: Nov 12 10-year 5.10%, compared with 4.98% on Nov 10 and 5.31% on Oct 5.
Nov 12 par yields: 2-year 4.86%, 30-year 5.43%; Nov 10: 4.73% and 5.35%, respectively.
Bond supply can pressure yields, while risk-off demand can pull them down; neither channel explains every daily move.

y10.say: The Treasury 10-year par yield rose from 4.98% on Nov 10 to 5.10% on Nov 12.

realy.label: Real yields

facts.text: Treasury real curve: Nov 12 10-year 2.86%, compared with 2.78% on Nov 10 and 2.95% on Oct 5.
An asset with no income faces an opportunity cost when real yields rise; haven demand may offset that channel.

realy.say: The Treasury 10-year real yield rose from 2.78% on Nov 10 to 2.86% on Nov 12.

boc.label: Bank of Canada
boc.value: BoC hiked to 2.50%; October jobless rate 6.7%

facts.text: Oct 28: the BoC raised its overnight target by 25 bp to 2.50% to reduce the risk that high energy costs spread to other prices.
The BoC said further increases may be needed but it will proceed carefully. Next scheduled decision: Dec 9.
Nov 6 release: October employment was little changed (−4,700), while unemployment rose to 6.7% from 6.5%.
September CPI was 3.1%, or 2.2% excluding gasoline.

boc.say: Canada has already hiked, but weaker employment makes the next decision harder.

energy.label: Energy stocks
energy.value: Nov 6: Energy among double-digit Q3 growth leaders

facts.text: Nov 6 FactSet: Energy was among the double-digit blended Q3 earnings-growth leaders. Overall S&P 500 growth was 31.4%, with 88% reported.

energy.say: Energy led in FactSet's Nov 6 blended Q3 earnings estimate; that is not a current stock return.

gold.label: Gold

facts.text: Nov 12 front-month Comex gold settled at $3,878.40 per troy ounce, its lowest settlement since Oct 2, 2025.
Higher real yields raise the cost of holding gold, but haven demand can offset this channel.

gold.say: Front-month gold settled at $3,878.40 on Nov 12; this is a futures price, not a spot quote.

credit.label: High-yield credit

facts.text: Nov 11 ICE BofA high-yield OAS: 3.30%, versus 3.34% on Nov 9.
Nov 11 ICE BofA CCC-and-lower OAS: 13.30%, versus 13.11% on Nov 9.

credit.say: Broad high-yield spreads narrowed between Nov 9 and Nov 11, while CCC-and-lower spreads widened.

semis.label: Semis & tech
semis.value: SOX 10,506.7 Nov 12; NVIDIA risk, peers diverge

facts.text: Nov 12 SOX close: 10,506.7, down 0.54% from 10,564.1 on Nov 11. Values use the displayed precision of Investing.com history.
Nov 5: SOX fell 12.25%. Reuters linked the AI selloff to fears that the election outcome could slow the data-center build-out.
Nov 12: AP reported other AI chip stocks rose while NVIDIA recovered part of its early loss. The leadership shock did not hit every chipmaker equally.

semis.say: The SOX and individual chip stocks can diverge; NVIDIA's CEO exit is a company shock.

cad.label: Canadian dollar

facts.text: Bank of Canada daily rate: USD/CAD 1.4255 on Nov 12, versus 1.4181 on Nov 10.
The BoC raised rates to 2.50% on Oct 28, but employment was little changed in October and unemployment rose to 6.7%.
A higher Canadian rate can support CAD at the margin; US rate expectations and risk appetite can outweigh that support.

cad.say: USD/CAD rose from 1.4181 on Nov 10 to 1.4255 on Nov 12; a higher quote means a weaker loonie.

sbcorr.label: Stock–bond corr.
sbcorr.value: Bonds cushioned the Nov 5 equity selloff

facts.text: Nov 5: the S&P 500 fell about 4.4% while short Treasury yields fell 12 bp. The curve bull-steepened during the tech selloff.
Apr 8: AQR describes stock-bond correlation as dependent on inflation versus growth uncertainty, rather than a permanent regime.
Nov 12: WSJ reported a Treasury selloff as Fed officials discussed higher interest rates to curb inflation.
These are dated hedge observations, not a new rolling-correlation estimate. Bond protection depends on whether growth risk or inflation dominates.

sbcorr.say: Bonds helped during the equity shock, but strong jobs and inflation can still challenge that hedge.

factor.label: Quality > momentum

facts.text: October ETF returns: iShares MSCI USA Quality Factor (QUAL) +0.1%; iShares MSCI USA Momentum Factor (MTUM) −10.5%, according to FactSet via MarketWatch.
MarketWatch reported investors favouring low debt and consistent earnings as AI stocks sold off in October.

factor.say: Quality held up better than momentum in October; treat that as a dated result, not a permanent relationship.

breadth.label: Equal vs cap weight

facts.text: September 30 to October 30 price returns: RSP +4.95% ($208.02 to $218.31); SPY -0.91% ($762.63 to $755.72).
24/7 Wall St. put technology near 37% of S&P 500 market value in its Nov 3 report, explaining why tech weakness hurts cap weight more.
October leadership is a completed-month comparison, not evidence that every stock held up in the Nov 5 selloff.
Nov 3 FactSet blended Q3 growth: Mag 7 22.6%, other 493 32.6%, with five of seven reported. If sustained, it would be their first slower quarter since Q4 2022.

breadth.say: Equal weight beat cap weight in October; that reduces concentration but does not remove market risk.

aipolicy.label: AI policy risk
aipolicy.value: Investors fear tighter AI infrastructure rules

facts.text: Nov 5: after the Democratic midterm sweep, investors feared Congress could slow the data-center build-out; the SOX fell about 12%.
This is a market assessment of future regulatory risk, not evidence that a new restriction has already taken effect.

aipolicy.say: The latest AI shock is a possible slowdown in data-center construction, priced before any new rules take effect.

nvidia.label: NVIDIA CEO resigns
nvidia.value: Nov 12 announcement: Huang out; Kress interim CEO

facts.text: Nov 12: NVIDIA announced Jensen Huang's departure as CEO, president and director. CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO.
The 8-K dates the board's acceptance of the resignation to Nov 11. Nov 12 is the public announcement date.
Nov 12: AP reported NVIDIA closed about 4% lower after dropping 14% at the opening bell.
NVIDIA kept Nov 17 for its fiscal Q3 2027 results, followed by an earnings call.

nvidia.say: NVIDIA's CEO exit adds leadership risk; the board expects product plans to continue.

leadership.label: AI leadership risk
leadership.value: NVIDIA succession risk; board expects continuity

facts.text: AP described Huang's departure as leaving NVIDIA facing an uncertain future.
NVIDIA's board expects operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap to continue without interruption.
Leadership uncertainty can affect the valuation investors pay for NVIDIA's earnings; it does not establish weaker chip demand across the sector.

leadership.say: Watch succession and execution at NVIDIA while keeping company risk separate from sector demand.

coreweave.label: CoreWeave earnings

facts.text: Nov 10: CoreWeave raised 2026 revenue guidance to $13.0–13.3B and guided full-year capex to $37–39B.
Q3 revenue was $3.661B versus $1.365B a year earlier.
Nov 11: CRWV rose 24.7%. Reuters said its report eased concerns about demand supporting debt-funded expansion.

coreweave.say: CoreWeave's results eased AI demand worries, while financing and construction risks remain.

chains.name: Is the bond hedge back?
chains.script: The bond hedge remains conditional. Reported attacks threaten Gulf energy deliveries, and Brent settled at $95.82 on Nov 12. Higher energy costs can feed inflation: October US CPI rose 0.4% on the month. Inflation pressure keeps tightening in focus despite the Fed's October hold. The 10-year Treasury par yield reached 5.10% on Nov 12, which can hurt both bond prices and equity valuations when inflation drives the move. Bonds did cushion the earlier November equity shock, so that episode is not proof of a permanent correlation regime. I would retain a growth-risk hedge while testing renewed oil inflation separately.

chains.name: Gold: haven versus rate risk
chains.script: Gold still faces competing haven and rate forces. Reported Gulf attacks can support oil and headline inflation, keeping pressure on the Fed after its October hold. The 10-year Treasury real yield rose to 2.86% on Nov 12, increasing the opportunity cost of a metal with no income. Front-month gold settled at $3,878.40 that day. This is a dated futures observation, not a spot quote. Haven demand can still offset the rate channel, so neither the price level nor one session proves a stable causal relationship. I would watch real yields and supply-risk headlines together.

chains.name: Who funds the AI build-out?
chains.script: AI investment still needs external capital. Amazon guides roughly $220B of cash capex this year, while its trailing free cash flow is negative. Meta combines equity and debt, including its November bond offering. CoreWeave reports $46.9B of debt carrying value; Anthropic proposes an IPO and a conditional private placement. Debt supply competes for capital, although Treasury refunding includes replacement borrowing rather than all new cash. Higher capital costs can slow construction, while higher discount rates can weigh on chip valuations. I would compare funding terms and cash generation with demand, rather than explain a daily Treasury move with issuance alone.

chains.name: AI earnings, rules and rotation
chains.script: AI construction risk has both demand support and policy headwinds. CoreWeave's Nov 10 results raised its 2026 revenue outlook to $13.0–13.3B, and CRWV rose 24.7% on Nov 11 as expansion worries eased. The earlier election shock points the other way: feared restrictions could slow data-center building and reduce expected chip demand. Because large technology companies dominate cap-weighted indices, chip weakness can favour equal weight. It can also favour strong balance sheets over crowded momentum; October factor returns are dated context. I would compare earnings guidance with actual construction rules before extrapolating either a relief rally or a selloff.

chains.name: Oil's winners and Canada's bind
chains.script: Canada faces energy inflation alongside a weak labour market. Brent rebounded to $95.82 on Nov 12, supporting the producer-earnings channel, although the week was still lower. FactSet placed Energy among the Q3 earnings-growth leaders; that dated blended estimate does not measure current stock performance. Higher energy prices can spread into other prices, which is why the BoC hiked to 2.50%. October unemployment was 6.7%. A higher Canadian rate can support the currency, but relative US expectations can offset it: the BoC daily USD/CAD rate was 1.4255 on Nov 12. I would watch relative policy expectations and oil together rather than treat a Canadian hike as a complete currency signal.

chains.name: Rotation to quality
chains.script: Balance-sheet strength matters when refinancing costs stay high. The Treasury 10-year par yield was 5.10% on Nov 12. Broad high-yield OAS narrowed to 3.30% on Nov 11, but CCC-and-lower OAS rose to 13.30%; those are spreads, not all-in borrowing yields. Higher refinancing costs can make low debt and dependable cash generation more valuable. October equity returns support that preference for that period: quality was roughly flat while momentum lost over 10%. I would apply the same discipline across credit and equities without assuming every quality stock is cheap or using an old factor return as today's forecast.

chains.name: NVIDIA's CEO exit and the index
chains.script: NVIDIA's CEO exit adds company risk to a concentrated market. The company announced Huang's departure on Nov 12 and named Colette Kress interim CEO. Succession uncertainty can reduce the valuation investors pay for NVIDIA's earnings, even if sector demand holds up. Through the largest chip names, that can affect a cap-weighted index more than equal weight. These valuation and concentration links are our reasoning. Other AI chip stocks rose that day, and NVIDIA's board expects its roadmap to continue without interruption. I would watch the permanent succession plan and the Nov 17 earnings call before assuming broader demand weakness.
